title: Telemetry event parameters must be bounded to enums, booleans, or None
answers: telemetry records free-form model flavor or URI scheme values
how do I add a new telemetry parameter without leaking user data
custom flavor shows up as its own name in usage tracking
bound the values of a usage event to a known set
body:
Invariant: every parameter an Event.parse returns must be a bool, None, or a value from a fixed, hand-maintained set. Anything outside the set becomes "other" (or "local" for a URI with no scheme).
Enforced in mlflow/telemetry/events.py:_bound_flavor (checks KNOWN_FLAVORS from mlflow/telemetry/constant.py), mlflow/telemetry/events.py:RegisterModelEvent.parse (env_pack checked against get_args(EnvPackType); source_scheme checked against _KNOWN_MODEL_URI_SCHEMES).
What breaks if skipped: free-form or user-identifying strings reach telemetry, and plugin-defined values inflate cardinality.
Constraints: do not bound against the artifact-repository registry, because plugins can register schemes at runtime. Parse schemes with urlparse so single-slash forms such as dbfs:/ classify as a scheme; splitting on '://' misclassifies them as local.
applies: Any Event subclass in mlflow/telemetry/events.py whose parse() reads user-supplied strings such as flavor, URI, or pack names.
says: Custom model flavors are appearing in usage tracking dashboards instead of being grouped as other.
Internal storage locations and private model paths are leaking into product telemetry reports.
Group all unrecognized model types under a single category in usage statistics.
Prevent proprietary storage scheme names from cluttering the model registry usage analytics.
search: Telemetry parameters returned by Event.parse must be bounded to bool, None, or values from fixed sets like KNOWN_FLAVORS, mapping anything outside to 'other' or 'local'. Applies to Event subclasses in mlflow/telemetry/events.py such as RegisterModelEvent.parse and _bound_flavor that parse user strings like flavor, URI schemes, or env_pack. Do not bound against the artifact-repository registry because plugins register schemes at runtime, and parse schemes with urlparse rather than splitting on '://' to properly classify single-slash schemes like dbfs:/.
